newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-FIORENTINA DARE TO DREAM OF GLORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FIORENTINA DARE TO DREAM OF GLORY.

text.p: In the five years since Gabriel Batistuta joined Fiorentina, fans have commissioned a statue and named a star after the Argentine striker.

When the purple-shirted hero helped the club take the Italian Cup last season and then scored twice to defeat league champions Milan at home in the pre-season `Supercoppa' last month, honorary citizenship was mooted.
Heaven knows what Fiorentina fans, among the most hot-tempered in Italy, will do if Batistuta helps the club win the title this season for the first time since 1969.
"Florence will be asking us to win every match," Batistuta admitted. "We must keep our feet on the ground."
"We don't have to win the "Scudetto" (title shield) at all costs but we will give it a try."

It may sound like a pipe dream in a country where the national sport has been dominated recently by the rich giants Milan and Juventus, but nobody is laughing at the suggestion that Fiorentina have what it takes to triumph.
"They are an excellent team. And they have the same outlook as last season," Juventus coach Marcello Lippi said.

With Italian clubs embarking on a buying spree in a radically changed European transfer market, the 1996-97 season which starts this weekend looks the most open for years with five or six clubs harbouring genuine hopes.
Milan and Juventus once again start as favourites but Fiorentina win the sentimental vote.

"There was once a purple butterfly with a sting," commented the Gazzetta dello Sport after the Supercoppa. "It was dangerous but it was still a butterfly. Today Florence has a strong team...what would once have been seen as a one-match wonder is now full of promise."
After losing 2-1 to Fiorentina, Milan were held 1-1 by second division Empoli in their opening cup match of the season and have to get used to new coach Oscar Tabarez.
Milan's player of the year George Weah has not looked his best pre-season, unlike Roberto Baggio who has been impressive but remains notoriously vulnerable to injury.
The team, winners of four league titles in the last five years, should be strengthened by Dutch international newcomers Edgar Davids and Michael Reiziger.

Juventus, the European Cup holders, also face a mountain of fixtures and have a rebuilt squad following the departures of captain Gianluca Vialli, Italian striker Fabrizio Ravanelli and Portuguese international midfielder Paulo Sousa.
Quiet French international striker Zinedine Zidane is the club's big investment with Croat Alen Boksic.
Juventus also have, in Lippi, the only coach active in serie A to have actually won the title.

Inter, chasing their first title since 1989, have completely revamped their squad with an influx of foreign players such as French international midfielder Youri Djourkaeff and Chilean striker Ivan Zamorano.
However their composure has been shattered by news that a heart problem diagnosed by Italian doctors may end the career of newly-signed Nigerian striker Nwankwo Kanu.
Lazio, already boasting two of Italy's deadliest attackers, have added Igor Protti alongside Giuseppe Signori and Italian international striker Pierluigi Casiraghi.

Parma, whose wealth puts them in the elite of Italian soccer, have bought striker Enrico Chiesa -- the sensational newcomer to the national team last season -- to partner established international Gianfranco Zola.

Chiesa is currently injured however and will almost certainly miss the club's opening match at home to Napoli on Saturday. The clash is one of four brought forward a day to allow teams time to prepare for UEFA Cup games next week.

The club, under new coach Carlo Ancelotti, looked completely out of sorts in losing 3-1 in the Italian Cup last month to second division Pescara. But the defeat will allow them to concentrate on UEFA Cup and league matches.
Fiorentina meanwhile have splashed out on Brazilian-born Belgian international Luis Oliveira from Cagliari and established Portuguese midfielder Rui Costa.
Piacenza are the only club without a single foreigner on their books, remaining proudly all-Italian.
Roma, who perennially flatter only to deceive, have a new coach in Argentine Carlos Bianchi.
At the bottom of the perceived pecking order, but not necessarily likely to remain there, are the serie A newcomers whose first aim is to avoid immediate relegation.
Bologna and Reggiana look to be the pick of the promoted clubs, with a question mark over Perugia and Verona.
Perugia, returning to the top for the first time in 15 years, managed the rare feat of imposing a press blackout on their players before the season has even started.
Veteran defender Pietro Vierchowod, who also left Juventus at the end of last season, walked out of Perugia last month saying he could not tolerate coach Giovanni Galeone.
"The fact is that I don't consider Galeone to be a serie A coach," said Vierchowod. "He has strange ideas."
